   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> - SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES</b> (Continued)</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Purchased loans are recorded at fair value at the time of acquisition and distinguished between purchased seasoned loans ("PSL"),&#160;purchased credit deteriorated loans ("PCD loans"), and non-seasoned new acquisitions. PSL are loans&#160;purchased at least <em style="font: inherit;">90</em> days after its original origination date and without significant credit deterioration. PCD loans are acquired loans that have experienced a more-than-insignificant decline in credit quality since their origination. We considered all loans that were currently <em style="font: inherit;">60</em> days or more past due, ever on nonaccrual status, had ever been past due <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> or more times, consumer loans with borrower credit scores below <em style="font: inherit;">600,</em>&#160;or commercial loans rated monitor, special mention,&#160;substandard or doubtful to be PCD loans.&#160;There were <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> non-seasoned new acquisition&#160;loans during <em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2023.</em>&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">PSL and PCD loans are accounted for&#160;using the gross-up approach prescribed in&#160;Accounting Standards Codification <em style="font: inherit;">326,</em> Financial Instruments - Credit Losses.&#160;The gross-up approach requires recognition of an allowance for the estimate of credit losses at the acquisition date. The allowance is recorded with an offsetting gross-up adjustment to the purchase price of the acquired financial asset.&#160;&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Accrued interest receivable on loans totaling $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631685" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableAccruedInterestAfterAllowanceForCreditLoss" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">17.5</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631686" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableAccruedInterestAfterAllowanceForCreditLoss" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">17.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, respectively, is included in other assets on the Consolidated Balance Sheets. We elected <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> to measure an allowance for accrued interest receivable and instead elected to reverse interest income on loans that are placed on nonaccrual status, which is generally when the loan becomes <em style="font: inherit;">90</em> days past due, or earlier if we believe the collection of interest is doubtful. We believe this policy results in the timely reversal of uncollectible interest.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Identified problem loans, which exhibit characteristics (financial or otherwise) that could cause the loans to become nonperforming or require restructuring in the future, are included on an internal watch list. Senior management and the Board of Directors review this list regularly. In some cases, we <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>determine that an individual loan exhibits unique risk characteristics that differentiate the loan from other loans within the loan segments. In such cases, the loans are evaluated for expected credit losses on an individual basis and excluded from the collective evaluation. Specific reserve allocations of the allowance for credit losses are determined by analyzing the borrower&#8217;s ability to repay amounts owed&#160;and collateral deficiencies, among other things.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">For individually analyzed loans that are deemed to be collateral dependent loans, we adopted the practical expedient to measure the allowance based on the fair value of collateral. The allowance is calculated on an individual loan basis based on the shortfall between the fair value of the loan&#8217;s collateral and its&#160;recorded principal balance. If the fair value of the collateral exceeds the recorded principal balance, <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> allowance is required. Fair value estimates of collateral on individually analyzed loans, as well as on foreclosed and repossessed assets, are reviewed periodically. We also have a process in place to monitor whether value estimates at each quarter-end are reflective of current market conditions. Our credit policies establish criteria for obtaining appraisals and determining internal value estimates. We <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>also adjust outside and internal valuations based on identifiable trends within our markets, such as recent sales of similar properties or assets, listing prices and offers received. In addition, we <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>discount certain appraised and internal value estimates to address distressed market conditions.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">We are also required to consider expected credit losses associated with loan commitments over the contractual period in which we are exposed to credit risk on the underlying commitments unless the obligation is unconditionally cancellable by us. Any allowance for off-balance sheet credit exposures is reported as an other liability on our Consolidated Balance Sheets and is increased or decreased via other noninterest expense on our Consolidated Statement of Income. The calculation includes consideration of the likelihood that funding will occur and forecasted credit losses on commitments expected to be funded over their estimated lives. The allowance is calculated using the same aggregate reserve rates calculated for the funded portion of loans at the portfolio level applied to the amount of commitments expected to be funded.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> - SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES</b> (Continued)</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:TransfersAndServicingOfFinancialAssetsPolicyTextBlock" id="c140640268" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Transfers of Financial Assets</span>: Transfers of financial assets are accounted for as sales when control over the assets has been surrendered. Control over transferred assets is deemed to be surrendered when: (<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>) the assets have been isolated from our banks and put presumptively beyond the reach of the transferor and its creditors, even in bankruptcy or other receivership, (<em style="font: inherit;">2</em>) the transferee obtains the right (free of conditions that constrain it from taking advantage of that right) to pledge or exchange the transferred assets, and (<em style="font: inherit;">3</em>) our banks do&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em> maintain effective control over the transferred assets through an agreement to repurchase them before their maturity or the ability to unilaterally cause the holder to return specific assets. Our transfers of financial assets are generally limited to commercial loan participations sold and residential mortgage loans sold in the secondary market.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentPolicyTextBlock" id="c140640269" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Premises and Equipment</span>: Land is carried at cost. Premises and equipment are stated at cost less accumulated depreciation. Buildings and related components are depreciated using the straight-line method with useful lives ranging from <em style="font: inherit;">5</em> to <em style="font: inherit;">33</em> years. Furniture, fixtures and equipment are depreciated using the straight-line method with useful lives ranging from <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> to <em style="font: inherit;">7</em> years. Maintenance, repairs and minor alterations are charged to current operations as expenditures occur and major improvements are capitalized. Premises and equipment are reviewed for impairment when events indicate their carrying amount <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be recoverable based on future undiscounted cash flows. If impaired, the assets are recorded at the lower of carrying value or fair value.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:FinanceLoanAndLeaseReceivablesHeldForInvestmentsForeclosedAssetsPolicy" id="c140640270" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Foreclosed Assets:</span> Assets acquired through or in lieu of foreclosure are initially recorded at their estimated fair value net of estimated selling costs, establishing a new cost basis. If fair value subsequently declines, a valuation allowance is recorded through noninterest expense, as are collection and operating costs after acquisition. We had <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> foreclosed assets as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="mbwm:BankOwnedLifeInsurancePolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c140640271" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Bank Owned Life Insurance:</span> Our banks have purchased life insurance policies on certain key officers. Bank owned life insurance is recorded at its cash surrender value, or the amount that can be realized. Increases in the net cash surrender value of the policies, as well as insurance proceeds received, are recorded as noninterest income on the Consolidated Statements of Income and are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> subject to income taxes.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:GoodwillAndIntangibleAssetsGoodwillPolicy" id="c140640272" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Goodwill</span>: The acquisition method of accounting requires that assets and liabilities acquired in a business combination to be&#160;recorded at fair value as of the acquisition date. The valuation of assets and liabilities often involves estimates based on <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party valuations or internal valuations based on discounted cash flow analyses or other valuation techniques, all of which are inherently subjective. This typically results in goodwill, the amount by which the cost of net assets acquired in a business combination exceeds their fair value, which is subject to impairment testing at least annually. We&#160;review&#160;goodwill for impairment on an annual basis as of <em style="font: inherit;"> October 1&#160;</em>or more often if events or circumstances indicate that it is more-likely-than-<em style="font: inherit;">not</em> that the fair value of a reporting unit is below its carrying value. Based on our annual impairment analysis of goodwill as of <em style="font: inherit;"> October 1, </em>it was determined that the fair value&#160;was in excess of its respective carrying value as of <em style="font: inherit;"> October 1, 2025; </em>therefore,&#160;goodwill was&#160;considered <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> impaired. Subsequent to the analysis of goodwill, on <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025,&#160;</em>we acquired Eastern Michigan Financial Corporation, resulting in the recognition of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631708" contextRef="d_2025-12-31_2025-12-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-EasternMichiganFinancialCorpMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:GoodwillAcquiredDuringPeriod" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">23.2</ix:nonFraction> million of goodwill. Goodwill recognized from the acquisition of Eastern Michigan Financial Corporation is&#160;further discussed in Note <em style="font: inherit;">17</em>&#160;-&#160;Business Combinations.&#160;&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:RepurchaseAndResaleAgreementsPolicy" id="c140640273" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Repurchase Agreements</span>: Our banks sell&#160;certain securities under agreements to repurchase. The agreements are treated as collateralized financing transactions, with the obligations to repurchase the securities sold reflected as liabilities and the securities underlying the agreements remaining in assets in the Consolidated Balance Sheets.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:OffBalanceSheetCreditExposurePolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c140640274" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Financial Instruments and Loan Commitments</span>: Financial instruments include off-balance-sheet credit instruments, such as commitments to make loans and commercial letters of credit, issued to meet customer financing needs. The face amount for these items represents the exposure to loss, before considering customer collateral or ability to repay. Such financial instruments are recorded when they are funded. Instruments, such as standby letters of credit, that are considered financial guarantees are recorded at fair value. Reserves for unfunded commitments are recorded as an other liability on our Consolidated Balance Sheets.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationOptionAndIncentivePlansPolicy" id="c140640275" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Stock-Based Compensation</span>: Compensation cost for equity-based awards is measured on the grant date based on the fair value of the award on&#160;that date&#160;and&#160;recognized over the requisite service period, net of estimated forfeitures. Fair value of stock option awards is estimated using a closed option valuation (Black-Scholes) model. Fair value of restricted stock awards is based upon the quoted market price of the common stock on the date of grant.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

        </div></div></div></ix:exclude></ix:nonNumeric><ix:exclude><div class="PGFTR" style="width: 100%;"><div class="hf-row"><div class="hf-cell" style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: center; margin: 0pt; width: calc(100% - 1px); display: inline-block;">(Continued)

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> </b>&#8211;<b> SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES </b>(Continued)</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerPolicyTextBlock" id="c140640276" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Revenue from Contracts with Customers</span>: We record revenue from contracts with customers in accordance with Accounting Standards Codification Topic <em style="font: inherit;">606,</em> &#8220;Revenue from Contracts with Customers&#8221; (&#8220;Topic <em style="font: inherit;">606&#8221;</em>). Under Topic <em style="font: inherit;">606,</em> we must identify the contract with a customer, identify the performance obligations in the contract, determine the transaction price, allocate the transaction price to the performance obligations in the contract, and recognize revenue when (or as) we satisfy a performance obligation. Significant revenue has <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> been recognized in the current reporting period that results from performance obligations satisfied in previous periods.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Our primary sources of revenue are derived from interest and dividends earned on loans, securities and other financial instruments that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> within the scope of Topic <em style="font: inherit;">606.</em> We have evaluated the nature of our contracts with customers and determined that further disaggregation of revenue from contracts with customers into more granular categories beyond what is presented in the Consolidated Statements of Income was <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> necessary.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">We generally satisfy our performance obligations on contracts with customers as services are rendered, and the transaction prices are typically fixed and charged either on a periodic basis (generally monthly) or based on activity. Because performance obligations are satisfied as services are rendered and the transaction prices are fixed, there is little judgment involved in applying Topic <em style="font: inherit;">606</em> that significantly affects the determination of the amount and timing of revenue from contracts with customers.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">The following table depicts our sources of noninterest income presented in the Consolidated Statements of Income for the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em> that are scoped within Topic <em style="font: inherit;">606:</em></p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Service Charges on Deposit and Sweep Accounts:</i> We earn fees from deposit and sweep customers for account maintenance, transaction-based and overdraft services. Account maintenance fees, which relate primarily to monthly maintenance, are earned over the course of the month reflecting the period over which we satisfy the performance obligation. Transaction-based fees, which include&#160;services such as stop payment and returned item charges, are recognized at the time the transaction is executed as that is the point in time we fulfill the customer request. Service charges on deposit and sweep accounts are withdrawn from the customer account balance.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Credit and Debit Card Fees:</i> We earn interchange income on our cardholder debit and credit card usage. Interchange income is primarily comprised of fees whenever our debit and credit cards are processed through card payment networks such as Visa. Interchange fees from cardholder transactions represent a percentage of the underlying transaction value and are recognized daily, concurrently with the transaction processing services provided to the cardholder.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Payroll Processing Fees:</i> We earn fees from providing payroll processing services for our commercial clients. Fees are assessed for processing weekly or bi-weekly payroll files, reports and documents, as well as year-end tax-related files, reports and documents. Fees are recognized and collected as payroll processing services are completed for each payroll run and year-end processing activities.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Customer Service Fees:</i> We earn fees by providing a variety of other services to our customers, such as wire transfers, check ordering, sales of cashier checks, and rentals of safe deposit boxes. Generally, fees are recognized and collected daily, concurrently with the point in time we fulfill the customer request. Safe deposit box rentals are on annual contracts, with fees generally earned at the time of the contract signing or renewal. Customer service fees are recorded as other noninterest income on our Consolidated Statements of Income.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:AdvertisingCostsPolicyTextBlock" id="c140640277" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Advertising Costs</span>: Advertising costs are expensed as incurred.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxPolicyTextBlock" id="c140640278" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Income Taxes</span>: Income tax expense is the total of the current year income tax due or refundable, the change in deferred income tax assets and liabilities, and any adjustments related to unrecognized tax benefits. Deferred income tax assets and liabilities are recognized for the tax consequences of temporary differences between the carrying amounts and tax bases of assets and liabilities, computed using enacted tax rates applicable to future years. A valuation allowance, if needed, reduces deferred income tax assets to the amount expected to be realized.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:FairValueOfFinancialInstrumentsPolicy" id="c140640279" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Fair Values of Financial Instruments</span>: Fair values of financial instruments are estimated using relevant market information and other assumptions. Fair value estimates involve uncertainties and matters of significant judgment regarding interest rates, credit risk, prepayments and other factors, especially in the absence of broad markets for particular items. Changes in assumptions or in market conditions could significantly affect the estimates. The fair value estimates of existing on- and off-balance sheet financial instruments do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> include the value of anticipated future business or the values of assets and liabilities <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> considered financial instruments.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:EarningsPerSharePolicyTextBlock" id="c140640280" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Earnings Per Share</span>: Basic earnings per share is based on the weighted average number of common shares and participating securities outstanding during the period. Diluted earnings per share include the dilutive effect of additional potential common shares issuable under our stock-based compensation plans using the treasury stock method. Our unvested stock awards, which contain non-forfeitable rights to dividends whether paid or unpaid (i.e., participating securities), are included in the number of shares outstanding for both basic and diluted earnings per share calculations. In the event of a net loss, our unvested stock awards are excluded from the calculations of both basic and diluted earnings per share.    <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:ComprehensiveIncomePolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c140640281" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Comprehensive Income (Loss)</span>: Comprehensive income (loss) consists of net income and other comprehensive income (loss).    <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:DerivativesPolicyTextBlock" id="c140640282" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Derivatives</span>: Derivative financial instruments are recognized as assets or liabilities at fair value. The accounting for changes in the fair value of derivatives depends on the use of the derivatives and whether the derivatives qualify for hedge accounting. Used as part of our asset and liability management to help manage interest rate risk, our derivatives have historically generally consisted of interest rate swap agreements that qualified for hedge accounting. We do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> use derivatives for trading purposes. Changes in the fair value of derivatives that are designated, for accounting purposes, as a hedge of the variability of cash flows to be received on various assets and liabilities and are effective are reported in other comprehensive income. They are later reclassified into earnings in the same periods during which the hedged transaction affects earnings and are included in the line item in which the hedged cash flows are recorded. If hedge accounting does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> apply, changes in the fair value of derivatives are recognized immediately in current earnings as interest income or expense. We had <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> derivative instruments designated as hedges as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:CommitmentsAndContingenciesPolicyTextBlock" id="c140640283" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Contingencies:</span> Loss contingencies, including claims and legal actions arising in the ordinary course of business, are recorded as liabilities when the likelihood of loss is probable and an amount or range of loss can be reasonably estimated. We do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> believe there are any such matters outstanding that would have a material effect on the financial statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c140640284" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Recent Accounting Changes Adopted</span>:&#160; Accounting Standards Updated <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">08,</em> <i>Financial Instruments - Credit Losses&#160;(Topic <em style="font: inherit;">326</em>): Purchased Loans.</i>&#160;This update&#160;expands the population of acquired financial instruments subject to the gross-up approach in Topic <em style="font: inherit;">326.</em> In accordance with the amendments in this update, loans (excluding credit cards) acquired without credit deterioration and deemed "seasoned" are purchased seasoned loans and accounted for using the gross-up approach at acquisition. This update takes effect for annual reporting periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026, </em>and interim reporting periods within those annual reporting periods with adoption being applied prospectively to loans that are acquired on or after the initial application date. We have adopted the standard and included the required disclosures in our financial statements.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> </b>&#8211;<b> SECURITIES</b> (Continued)</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">We evaluate securities in an unrealized loss position at least quarterly. Consideration is given to the financial condition of the issuer, and the intent and ability we have to retain our investment in the issuer for a period of time sufficient to allow for any anticipated recovery in fair value. For those debt securities whose fair value is less than their amortized cost basis, we also consider our intent to sell the security, whether it is more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> that we will be required to sell the security before recovery and if we do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expect to recover the entire amortized cost basis of the security. In analyzing an issuer&#8217;s financial condition, we <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>consider whether the securities are issued by the federal government or its agencies, whether downgrades by bond rating agencies have occurred and the results of reviews of the issuer&#8217;s financial condition.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">At <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, <ix:nonFraction id="c140631757" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleUnrealizedLossPositionNumberOfPositions" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">607</ix:nonFraction> debt securities with estimated fair values totaling $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631758" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleUnrealizedLossPosition" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">545</ix:nonFraction> million had unrealized losses aggregating $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631759" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleUnrealizedLossPositionAccumulatedLoss" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">36.9</ix:nonFraction> million. At <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em>, <ix:nonFraction id="c140631760" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleUnrealizedLossPositionNumberOfPositions" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">843</ix:nonFraction>&#160;debt securities with estimated fair values totaling $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631761" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleUnrealizedLossPosition" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">680</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million had unrealized losses aggregating $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631762" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleUnrealizedLossPositionAccumulatedLoss" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">63.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million. At <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, unrealized losses aggregating $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631763" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_FinancialInstrumentAxis-BondsIssuedOrGuaranteedByAgenciesOfTheUSFederalGovernmentMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleUnrealizedLossPositionAccumulatedLoss" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">31.1</ix:nonFraction> million were attributable to bonds issued or guaranteed by agencies of the U.S. federal government, while unrealized losses totaling $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631764" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_FinancialInstrumentAxis-BondsIssuedByStatebasedMunicipalitiesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleUnrealizedLossPositionAccumulatedLoss" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">5.7</ix:nonFraction> million were associated with bonds issued by state-based municipalities. After considering the issuers of the bonds&#160;and taking into account the fact that <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> municipal issuer had been subject to a credit rating downgrade by bond credit rating agencies, we determined that the unrealized losses were due to changing interest rate environments. As we do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> intend to sell our debt securities before recovery of their cost basis and we believe it is more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> that we will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be required to sell our debt securities before recovery of the cost basis, <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> unrealized losses are deemed to represent credit losses.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">The amortized cost and fair values of debt securities at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, by maturity, are shown in the following table.    <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">The carrying value of U.S. Government agency debt obligations and mortgage-backed securities that are pledged to secure repurchase agreements was $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631781" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_FinancialInstrumentAxis-UsGovernmentAgencyDebtObligationsAndMortgageBackedSecuritiesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleRestricted" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">232</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631782" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_FinancialInstrumentAxis-UsGovernmentAgencyDebtObligationsAndMortgageBackedSecuritiesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleRestricted" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">122</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, respectively. The carrying value of U.S. Government agency debt obligations that are pledged to secure specific customer deposits was&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c140631784" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_FinancialInstrumentAxis-USGovernmentAgenciesDebtSecuritiesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleRestricted" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">12.6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631785" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_FinancialInstrumentAxis-USGovernmentAgenciesDebtSecuritiesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleRestricted" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">11.7</ix:nonFraction> million as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, respectively.&#160;</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:LoansNotesTradeAndOtherReceivablesDisclosureTextBlock" id="c3113578" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> </b>&#8211;<b> LOANS AND ALLOWANCE FOR CREDIT LOSSES</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Commercial loans are divided among <em style="font: inherit;">five</em> segments based primarily on collateral type, risk characteristics, and primary and secondary sources of repayment. These segments are then further stratified based on the commercial loan grade that is assigned using our standard loan grading paradigm. Retail loans are divided into <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> of <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> groups based on risk characteristics and source of repayment. Our allowance for credit loss pools are consistent with those used for loan note disclosure purposes.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Our loan portfolio segments as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em> were as follows:</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:36pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">o</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Commercial Loans</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:72pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9632;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Commercial and Industrial</span>: Risks to this loan category include industry concentration and the practical limitations associated with monitoring the condition of the collateral which often consists of inventory, accounts receivable, and other non-real estate assets. Equipment and inventory obsolescence can also pose a risk. Declines in general economic conditions and other events can cause cash flows to fall to levels insufficient to service debt.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:72pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9632;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Owner Occupied Commercial Real Estate</span>: Risks to this loan category include industry concentration and the inability to monitor the condition of the collateral. Declines in general economic conditions and other events can cause cash flows to fall to levels insufficient to service debt. Also, declines in real estate values and lack of suitable alternative use for the properties are risks for loans in this category.</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:72pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9632;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Non-Owner Occupied Commercial Real Estate</span>: Loans in this category are susceptible to declines in occupancy rates, business failure, and general economic conditions. Also, declines in real estate values and lack of suitable alternative use for the properties are risks for loans in this category.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:72pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9632;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Multi-Family and Residential Rental</span>: Risks to this loan category include industry concentration and the inability to monitor the condition of the collateral. Loans in this category are susceptible to weakening general economic conditions and increases in unemployment rates, as well as market demand and supply of similar property and the resulting impact on occupancy rates, market rents, cash flow, and income-based real estate values. Also, the lack of a suitable alternative use for the properties is a risk for loans in this category.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:72pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9632;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Vacant Land, Land Development and Residential Construction</span>: Risks common to commercial construction loans are cost overruns, changes in market demand for property, inadequate long-term financing arrangements, and declines in real estate values. Residential construction loans are susceptible to those same risks as well as those associated with residential mortgage loans. Changes in market demand for property could lead to longer marketing times resulting in higher carrying costs, declining values, and higher interest rates.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:54pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">o</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Retail Loans</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:72pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9632;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; "><em style="font: inherit;">1</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">4</em> Family Mortgages</span>: Residential mortgage loans are susceptible to weakening general economic conditions and increases in unemployment rates and declining real estate values.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:72pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9632;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Other Consumer Loans</span>: Risks common to these loans include regulatory risks, unemployment, and changes in local economic conditions as well as the inability to monitor collateral consisting of personal property.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">Nonaccrual loans represent the entire balance of collateral dependent loans. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, all collateral dependent loans were secured by real estate, with the exception of those classified as commercial and industrial, which were secured by accounts receivable, inventory, and equipment.&#160;Interest income recognized on nonaccrual loans totaled $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631801" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableNonaccrualInterestIncome" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">1.0</ix:nonFraction> million in <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>,&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c140631803" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableNonaccrualInterestIncome" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million in&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>&#160;and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631805" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableNonaccrualInterestIncome" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million in <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>, reflecting the collection of interest at the time of principal pay-off.&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> </b>&#8211;<b> LOANS AND ALLOWANCE FOR CREDIT LOSSES</b> (Continued)</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Credit Quality Indicators.</i> We utilize a comprehensive grading system for our commercial loans. All commercial loans are graded on a <em style="font: inherit;">ten</em> grade rating system. The rating system utilizes standardized grade paradigms that analyze several critical factors such as cash flow, operating performance, financial condition, collateral, industry condition and management. All commercial loans are reviewed and graded at inception and, if appropriate, re-graded at various intervals thereafter. The risk assessment for retail loans is primarily based on the type of collateral.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">All commercial loans are graded using the following criteria:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 54pt;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Grade <em style="font: inherit;">1.</em></p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#8220;Exceptional&#8221;&#160;&#160;Loans with this rating contain very little, if any, risk.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 54pt;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Grade <em style="font: inherit;">2.</em></p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#8220;Outstanding&#8221;&#160;&#160;Loans with this rating have excellent and stable sources of repayment and conform to bank policy and regulatory requirements.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 54pt;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Grade <em style="font: inherit;">3.</em></p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#8220;Very Good&#8221;&#160;&#160;Loans with this rating have strong sources of repayment and conform to bank policy and regulatory requirements. These are loans for which repayment risks are acceptable.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 54pt;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Grade <em style="font: inherit;">4.</em></p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#8220;Good&#8221;&#160;&#160;Loans with this rating have solid sources of repayment and conform to bank policy and regulatory requirements. These are loans for which repayment risks are modest.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 54pt;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Grade <em style="font: inherit;">5.</em></p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#8220;Acceptable&#8221;&#160;&#160;Loans with this rating exhibit acceptable sources of repayment and conform with most bank policies and all regulatory requirements. These are loans for which repayment risks are satisfactory.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 54pt;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Grade <em style="font: inherit;">6.</em></p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#8220;Monitor&#8221;&#160;&#160;Loans with this rating are considered to have emerging weaknesses which <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>include negative current cash flow, high leverage, or operating losses. Generally, if further deterioration is observed, these credits will be downgraded to the criticized asset report.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 54pt;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Grade <em style="font: inherit;">7.</em></p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#8220;Special Mention&#8221;&#160;&#160;Loans with this rating have potential weaknesses that deserve management&#8217;s close attention. If left uncorrected, these potential weaknesses <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>result in deterioration of the repayment prospects for the loan at some future date.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 54pt;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Grade <em style="font: inherit;">8.</em></p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#8220;Substandard&#8221;&#160;&#160;Loans with this rating are inadequately protected by current sound net worth, paying capacity of the obligor, or of the pledged collateral, if any. A Substandard loan normally has <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> or more well-defined weaknesses that jeopardize the repayment of the debt. They are characterized by the distinct possibility of loss if the deficiencies are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> corrected.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 54pt;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Grade <em style="font: inherit;">9.</em></p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#8220;Doubtful&#8221;&#160;&#160;Loans with this rating exhibit all the weaknesses inherent in the Substandard classification and where collection or liquidation in full is highly questionable and improbable.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 54pt;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Grade <em style="font: inherit;">10.</em></p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#8220;Loss&#8221;&#160;&#160;Loans with this rating are considered uncollectable, and of such little value that continuance as an active asset is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> warranted.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">The primary risk elements with respect to commercial loans are the financial condition of the borrower, the sufficiency of collateral, and timeliness of scheduled payments. We have a policy of requesting and reviewing periodic financial statements from commercial loan customers and employ a disciplined and formalized review of the existence of collateral and its value. The primary risk element with respect to each residential real estate loan and consumer loan is the timeliness of scheduled payments; loans <em style="font: inherit;">90</em> days or more past due are considered nonperforming. We have a reporting system that monitors past due loans and have adopted policies to pursue creditors&#8217; rights in order to preserve our collateral position.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> </b>&#8211;<b> LOANS AND ALLOWANCE FOR CREDIT LOSSES</b> (Continued)</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Mercantile Bank uses a migration to loss methodology to determine historical loss rates for commercial loans given the comprehensive loan grading process employed by Mercantile Bank for over <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> decades, while an open pool approach is best suited for retail loans given the smaller dollar size of the segments. A baseline loss rate is produced at each reporting date for each loan portfolio segment using bank-specific loan charge-off and recovery data over a defined historical look-back period. The look-back period represents the number of data periods that will be used to calculate a baseline loss rate for each loan portfolio segment. We determined that the look-back period commencing on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2011 </em>through the reporting date was reasonable and appropriate for the calculation of historical loss rates for&#160;both&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Mercantile Bank's historical loss rate is then applied to future loan balances at the instrument level based on remaining contractual life adjusted for amortization, prepayment and default to develop a baseline lifetime loss. Our prepayment speed assumptions are developed at the loan segment level based upon the consideration of all relevant data in which we believe will&#160;impact anticipated customer behavior including changes in interest rates, economic conditions, and underlying property valuations. For the commercial loan portfolio segments, we assumed a <ix:nonFraction id="c140631842" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis-CommercialPortfolioSegmentMember" unitRef="Pure" name="mbwm:FinancingReceivablesPrepaymentSpeedAssumed" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">2</ix:nonFraction>% prepayment speed as of both <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> as we deemed there to be <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> considerable changes from historical experience. For the retail <em style="font: inherit;">1</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">4</em> family mortgage and retail other consumer portfolios, we increased&#160;the&#160;prepayment speed from <ix:nonFraction id="c140631847" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis-RetailPortfolioSegmentMember_FinancingReceivableRecordedInvestmentByClassOfFinancingReceivableAxis-OneToFourFamilyMortgagesMember" unitRef="Pure" name="mbwm:FinancingReceivablesPrepaymentSpeedAssumed" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">7.8</ix:nonFraction>% as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em> to <ix:nonFraction id="c140631848" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis-RetailPortfolioSegmentMember_FinancingReceivableRecordedInvestmentByClassOfFinancingReceivableAxis-OneToFourFamilyMortgagesMember" unitRef="Pure" name="mbwm:FinancingReceivablesPrepaymentSpeedAssumed" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">9.5</ix:nonFraction>% as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>. This increase&#160;shortened the average lives of the portfolios in which the loss rates were applied, resulting in a decrease to the allowance of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631849" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis-RetailPortfolioSegmentMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableAllowanceForCreditLossesPeriodIncreaseDecrease" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5" sign="-">2.3</ix:nonFraction> million. This change in assumption was driven by lower long-term interest rates and the compositions of the underlying portfolios.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">During each reporting period, we also consider the need to adjust the historical loss rates as determined to reflect the extent to which we expect current conditions and reasonable and supportable economic forecasts to differ from the conditions that existed for the period over which the historical loss information was determined. These qualitative adjustments <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>increase or decrease our estimate of expected future credit losses. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, we used a <em style="font: inherit;">one</em>-year reasonable and supportable economic forecast period, with a <em style="font: inherit;">six</em>-month straight-line reversion period for all loan segments. The economic forecasts used for our&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>&#160;allowance calculations reflected&#160;allowance balance reductions of&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c140631854" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="mbwm:FinancingReceivableAllowanceForCreditLossPeriodIncreaseDecreaseFromForecastChanges" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5" sign="-">0.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c140631855" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="mbwm:FinancingReceivableAllowanceForCreditLossPeriodIncreaseDecreaseFromForecastChanges" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5" sign="-">2.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">The allowance for PSL and PCD loans acquired from the acquisition of Eastern Michigan Bank were measured at the loan segment level using proxy expected lifetime loss rates adjusted for qualitative risk factors, including lending management experience, loan review and audit results, asset quality and portfolio trends, loan portfolio growth, industry concentrations, trends in underlying collateral, external factors, and economic conditions <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> already captured.&#160;&#160;&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Individual loans exhibiting unique risk characteristics, which differentiate the loans from other loans within the loan segments and are evaluated for expected credit losses on an individual basis, totaled $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631857" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableIndividuallyEvaluatedForImpairment" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">7.9</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631858" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableIndividuallyEvaluatedForImpairment" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">7.4</ix:nonFraction> million as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, respectively. Individual allowance allocations totaled $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631860" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="mbwm:FinancingReceivableAllowanceForCreditLossesIndividuallyEvaluatedForImpairment" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">4.0</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631861" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="mbwm:FinancingReceivableAllowanceForCreditLossesIndividuallyEvaluatedForImpairment" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.2</ix:nonFraction> million as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Depreciation expense totaled $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631872" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:Depreciation" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">5.2</ix:nonFraction> million for&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631874" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:Depreciation" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">6.0</ix:nonFraction> million for both&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>&#160;and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">We enter into facility leases in the normal course of business. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, we were under lease contracts for <em style="font: inherit;">eleven</em> of our branch facilities. The leases have maturity dates ranging from <em style="font: inherit;"> August, 2026&#160;</em>through <em style="font: inherit;"> May, 2048, </em>with a weighted average life of <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseWeightedAverageRemainingLeaseTerm1" id="c140631878" format="ixt-sec:duryear">9.4</ix:nonNumeric> years as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>. All of our leases have multiple <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140631879">three</span>- to <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140631880">five</span>-year extensions; however, these were <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> factored in the lease maturities and weighted average lease term as it is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> reasonably certain we will exercise the options.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Leases are classified as either operating or finance leases at the lease commencement date, with all of our current leases determined to be operating leases. Lease expense for operating leases is recognized on a straight-line basis over the lease term. Right-of-use assets represent our right to use an underlying asset for the lease term, while lease liabilities represent our obligation to make lease payments arising from the lease. Right-of-use assets and lease liabilities are recognized at the lease commencement date at the estimated present value of lease payments over the lease term. We use our incremental borrowing rate, on a collateralized basis, at lease commencement to calculate the present value of lease payments. The weighted average discount rate for leases was <ix:nonFraction id="c140631883" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseWeightedAverageDiscountRatePercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">6.52</ix:nonFraction>% as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">The right-of-use assets, included in <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140632516"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140632517">premises and equipment, net</span></span> on our Consolidated Balance Sheets, and the lease liabilities, included in <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140632518"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140632519">other liabilities</span></span> on our Consolidated Balance Sheets, totaled $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631884" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseRightOfUseAsset" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">3.9</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631885" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseRightOfUseAsset" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">4.4</ix:nonFraction> million as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em>, respectively. As permitted by applicable accounting standards, we have elected <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> to recognize short-term leases with original terms of <em style="font: inherit;">twelve</em> months or less on our Consolidated Balance Sheets. Total operating lease expense associated with the leases aggregated $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631888" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631889" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631890" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">2.0</ix:nonFraction> million in <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>,&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>, respectively.</p>
