   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Mortgage servicing rights result from our mortgage loan origination activities. Late and ancillary fees, included as part of mortgage banking income and reported as noninterest income in the Consolidated Statements of Income, aggregated less than $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631902" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" unitRef="USD" name="mbwm:LateAndAncillaryFeeIncomeGeneratedByServicingFinancialAssetsAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.1</ix:nonFraction> million during <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">We determined that <ix:nonFraction id="c140631905" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ValuationAllowanceForImpairmentOfRecognizedServicingAssetsBalance" scale="6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> valuation allowance was necessary as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em> or <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em>. The estimated fair value of mortgage servicing rights was $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631906" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ServicingAssetAtFairValueAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">21.4</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631907" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ServicingAssetAtFairValueAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">21.0</ix:nonFraction> million as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, respectively. The fair value of mortgage servicing rights is estimated using a valuation model that calculates the present value of estimated future net servicing cash flows, taking into consideration expected mortgage loan prepayment rates, discount rates, servicing costs and other economic factors, which are determined based on current market conditions. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, fair value was determined using a discount rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c140631909" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:ServicingAssetsAndServicingLiabilitiesAtFairValueAssumptionsUsedToEstimateFairValueDiscountRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">10.00</ix:nonFraction>%,&#160;a weighted average constant prepayment rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c140631910" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:ServicingAssetsAndServicingLiabilitiesAtFairValueAssumptionsUsedToEstimateFairValuePrepaymentSpeed" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">9.13</ix:nonFraction>%, depending on the stratification of the specific right, and a weighted average delinquency rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c140631911" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:ServicingAssetsAndServicingLiabilitiesAtFairValueAssumptionsUsedToEstimateFairValueExpectedCreditLosses" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">0.76</ix:nonFraction>%. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em>, fair value was determined using a discount rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c140631912" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:ServicingAssetsAndServicingLiabilitiesAtFairValueAssumptionsUsedToEstimateFairValueDiscountRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">10.50</ix:nonFraction>%, a weighted average constant prepayment rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c140631913" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:ServicingAssetsAndServicingLiabilitiesAtFairValueAssumptionsUsedToEstimateFairValuePrepaymentSpeed" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">7.81</ix:nonFraction>%, depending on the stratification of the specific right, and a weighted average delinquency rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c140631914" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:ServicingAssetsAndServicingLiabilitiesAtFairValueAssumptionsUsedToEstimateFairValueExpectedCreditLosses" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">0.68</ix:nonFraction>%.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">The weighted average amortization period was <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:ServicingAssetsAndServicingLiabilitiesAtFairValueAssumptionsUsedToEstimateFairValueWeightedAverageLife1" id="c140631915" format="ixt-sec:duryear">8.2</ix:nonNumeric> years and <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" name="us-gaap:ServicingAssetsAndServicingLiabilitiesAtFairValueAssumptionsUsedToEstimateFairValueWeightedAverageLife1" id="c140631916" format="ixt-sec:duryear">8.7</ix:nonNumeric>&#160;years as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, respectively.&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Securities sold under agreements to repurchase (&#8220;repurchase agreements&#8221;) generally have original maturities of less than <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140631931">one</span> year. Repurchase agreements are treated as financings, and the obligations to repurchase securities sold are reflected as liabilities on our Consolidated Balance Sheets. Repurchase agreements are secured by securities with an aggregate fair value equal to the aggregate outstanding balance of the repurchase agreements. The securities, which are included in securities available for sale on our Consolidated Balance Sheets, are held in safekeeping by a correspondent bank. Repurchase agreements are offered principally to certain large deposit customers.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Our unamortized debt issuance costs were $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631963" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-SubordinatedNotesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredFinanceCostsGross" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631964" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-SubordinatedNotesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredFinanceCostsGross" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.7</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, respectively.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> December 24, 2025, </em>we&#160;entered into a credit agreement&#160;with U.S. Bank National Association&#160;for a $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631966" contextRef="i_2025-12-24_DebtInstrumentAxis-TermNoteMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">30.0</ix:nonFraction> million term note.&#160;The term loan bears interest at an annual rate equal to <ix:nonFraction id="c140631967" contextRef="i_2025-12-24_DebtInstrumentAxis-TermNoteMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">1.70</ix:nonFraction>% plus the greater of (a) <em style="font: inherit;">zero</em> percent (<ix:nonFraction id="c140631969" contextRef="d_2025-12-24_2025-12-24_DebtInstrumentAxis-TermNoteMember_RangeAxis-MinimumMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentBasisSpreadOnVariableRate1" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">0.0</ix:nonFraction>%) and (b) the <em style="font: inherit;">one</em>-month forward-looking term rate based on SOFR. Interest and principal are payable beginning <em style="font: inherit;"> March 15, 2026, </em>and on the same date of each <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> month thereafter, plus a final payment equal to all unpaid interest and principal. Principal shall be paid in installments of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631972" contextRef="d_2025-12-24_2025-12-24_DebtInstrumentAxis-TermNoteMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentPeriodicPaymentPrincipal" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.5</ix:nonFraction> million each. The term loan matures on <em style="font: inherit;"> December 24, 2028. </em>Mercantile is permitted to prepay the term note evidencing the term loan in full or in part at any time without indemnity, premium or penalty.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em>we had net operating loss carryforwards of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140631983" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-EasternMichiganFinancialCorpMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">7.3</ix:nonFraction> million related to the acquisition of Eastern Michigan Financial Corporation. The ability to utilize the net operating loss&#160;in future periods is limited based on the value of Eastern Michigan Financial Corporation's value at the time of the ownership change and applicable federal rates.&#160;A valuation allowance related to deferred tax assets is required when it is considered more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> that all or part of the benefits related to such assets will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be realized. We determined that <ix:nonFraction id="c140631986" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowance" scale="6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> valuation allowance was required at year-end <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> or&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">We had <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140631989"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140632554">no</span></span> unrecognized tax benefits at any time during&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> or&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>. Should the accrual of any interest or penalties relative to unrecognized tax benefits be necessary, it is our policy to record such accruals in our income tax accounts; <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140631992">no</span> such accruals existed at any time during <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> or&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>. We are <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> longer&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">no</em> longer subject to examination by taxing authorities for&#160;years before <em style="font: inherit;">2022.</em></p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>&#160;</b>&#8211;<b> STOCK-BASED COMPENSATION</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 0pt;">Stock-based compensation plans are used to provide directors and employees with an increased incentive to contribute to our long-term performance and growth, to align the interests of directors and employees with the interests of our shareholders through the opportunity for increased stock ownership and to attract and retain directors and employees.&#160;Stock-based compensation, reported as noninterest expense in the Consolidated Statements of Income, totaled $<ix:nonFraction id="c140632000" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_IncomeStatementLocationAxis-NoninterestExpenseMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">3.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, $<ix:nonFraction id="c140632001" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31_IncomeStatementLocationAxis-NoninterestExpenseMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">3.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140632002" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31_IncomeStatementLocationAxis-NoninterestExpenseMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">3.4</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million in <em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;">2023,</em> respectively. The&#160;Stock Incentive Plan of <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em> that was approved by shareholders in <em style="font: inherit;"> May, 2023.&#160;</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt;">Under the&#160;Stock Incentive Plan of <em style="font: inherit;">2023,</em> incentive awards <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>include, but are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> limited to, stock options, restricted stock, stock appreciation rights and stock awards. Incentive awards that are stock options or stock appreciation rights are granted with an exercise price <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> less than the closing price of our common stock on the date of grant.&#160; Price, vesting and expiration date parameters are determined by Mercantile&#8217;s Compensation Committee on a grant-by-grant basis.&#160; <em style="font: inherit;">No</em> payments are required from employees for restricted stock awards.&#160; The restricted stock awards granted during the years <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>&#160;through <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;fully vest after <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> years and, in the case of performance-based restricted stock issued to executive officers in <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>&#160;through <em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em> are subject to the attainment of pre-determined performance goals.&#160; At year-end <em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em> there were approximately <ix:nonFraction id="c140632017" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">292,600</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares authorized for future incentive awards.</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">12</em>&#160;</b>&#8211;<b> COMMITMENTS AND OFF-BALANCE-SHEET RISK </b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">We are a party to financial instruments with off-balance sheet risk in the normal course of business to meet the financing needs of our customers. These financial instruments include commitments to extend credit and standby letters of credit. Loan commitments to extend credit are agreements to lend to a customer as long as there is <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> violation of any condition established in the contract. Standby letters of credit are conditional commitments issued by our banks to guarantee the performance of a customer to a <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> party. Commitments generally have fixed expiration dates or other termination clauses and <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>require payment of a fee. Since many of the commitments are expected to expire without being drawn upon, the total commitment amounts do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> necessarily represent future cash requirements.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">These instruments involve, to varying degrees, elements of credit risk in excess of the amount recognized, if any, in the balance sheet. Our maximum exposure to loan loss in the event of nonperformance by the other party to the financial instrument for commitments to extend credit and standby letters of credit is represented by the contractual notional amount of those instruments. We use the same credit policies in making commitments and conditional obligations as we do for on-balance sheet instruments. Collateral, such as accounts receivable, securities, inventory, and property and equipment, is generally obtained based on management&#8217;s credit assessment of the borrower.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">We are required to consider expected credit losses associated with loan commitments over the contractual period in which we are exposed to credit risk on the underlying commitments unless the obligation is unconditionally cancellable by us. Any allowance for off-balance sheet credit exposures is reported as an other liability on our Consolidated Balance Sheets and is increased or decreased via other noninterest expense on our Consolidated Statements of Income. The calculation includes consideration of the likelihood that funding will occur and forecasted credit losses on commitments expected to be funded over their estimated lives. The allowance is calculated using the same aggregate reserve rates calculated for the funded portion of loans at the portfolio level applied to the amount of commitments expected to be funded.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">For commercial lines of credit, retail lines of credit and credit card average outstanding balances, we determined&#160;allowance requirements by calculating the difference between the average percent outstanding of the funded commitments over the past several years to actual percent outstanding at period end and applying the respective expected loss allocation factors to the difference as this difference represents the average of unfunded commitments we expect to eventually be drawn upon. For commitments to make loans, we determine an allowance by applying the expected loss allocation factor to&#160;the amount expected to fund.&#160;The calculated allowance aggregated $<ix:nonFraction id="c140632044" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_FinancingReceivableRecordedInvestmentByClassOfFinancingReceivableAxis-RetailAndCommercialLinesOfCreditAndCreditCardReceivablesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableAllowanceForCreditLosses" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140632045" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_FinancingReceivableRecordedInvestmentByClassOfFinancingReceivableAxis-RetailAndCommercialLinesOfCreditAndCreditCardReceivablesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableAllowanceForCreditLosses" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">1.0</ix:nonFraction> million as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, respectively. We do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> reserve for residential mortgage construction loans, as the loans are for <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> year or less and draws are governed by the receipt and satisfactory review of contractor and subcontractor sworn statements, lien waivers and title insurance company endorsements. Letters of credit are rarely drawn.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Commitments to make commercial loans generally reflect our binding obligations to existing and prospective customers to extend credit, including line of credit facilities secured by accounts receivable and inventory, and term loans&#160;secured by either real estate or equipment.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">In most instances, commercial line of credit facilities have&#160;terms ranging from <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_FinancingReceivableRecordedInvestmentByClassOfFinancingReceivableAxis-CommercialLineOfCreditFacilitiesMember_RangeAxis-MinimumMember" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityExpirationPeriod" id="c140632053" format="ixt-sec:durmonth">12</ix:nonNumeric> to <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_FinancingReceivableRecordedInvestmentByClassOfFinancingReceivableAxis-CommercialLineOfCreditFacilitiesMember_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityExpirationPeriod" id="c140632054" format="ixt-sec:durmonth">24</ix:nonNumeric> months with&#160;floating rates tied to the Wall Street Journal Prime Rate or <em style="font: inherit;">30</em>-Day SOFR. Commercial term loans secured by real estate are generally at a floating rates tied to the Wall Street Journal Prime Rate or&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">30</em>-Day SOFR. Since the <em style="font: inherit;">fourth</em> quarter of <em style="font: inherit;">2020,</em> a fixed rate option for commercial term loans secured by real estate is generally <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> offered for loans over <em style="font: inherit;">$2.5</em> million; instead, customers are offered participation in our back-to-back interest rate swap program to achieve a desired fixed rate. For loans under <em style="font: inherit;">$2.5</em> million, we offer a rate primarily equal to the commensurate cost of funds using FHLBI advance rates as a proxy and a credit spread as indicated by the credit rating we assign. Commercial term loans&#160;secured by real estate generally balloon within <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140632062">five</span> years, with payments based on amortizations ranging from <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_RangeAxis-MinimumMember" name="mbwm:AmortizationPeriodForTermDebtSecuredByRealEstate" id="c140632063" format="ixt-sec:duryear">10</ix:nonNumeric> to <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" name="mbwm:AmortizationPeriodForTermDebtSecuredByRealEstate" id="c140632064" format="ixt-sec:duryear">25</ix:nonNumeric> years. Commercial term loans secured by non-real estate collateral are&#160;generally at a floating rate tied to the Wall Street Journal Prime Rate&#160;or <em style="font: inherit;">30</em>-Day SOFR, or a fixed rate primarily equal to the commensurate cost of funds using FHLBI advance rates as a proxy and a credit spread as indicated by the credit rating we assign, and generally mature and fully amortize within <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140632066">three</span> to <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140632067">seven</span> years.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">The following standby letters of credit are considered financial guarantees under current accounting guidance. These instruments are carried at fair value as an other liability on our Consolidated Balance Sheets. Standby letters of credit are generally cross collateralized with the borrowers&#8217; other loans with us, and are included in our borrower collateral analyses.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">13</em>&#160;</b>&#8211;<b> BENEFIT PLANS</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">We have a <em style="font: inherit;">401</em>(k) benefit plan that covers substantially all of our employees. The percent of our matching contributions to the <em style="font: inherit;">401</em>(k) benefit plan is determined annually by the Board of Directors. The matching contribution has been <ix:nonFraction id="c140632072" contextRef="d_2018-04-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanEmployerMatchingContributionPercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">5.00</ix:nonFraction>% since <em style="font: inherit;"> April 1, 2018. </em>Matching contributions, if made, are immediately vested. Our <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>,&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2023</em> matching <em style="font: inherit;">401</em>(k) contributions charged to expense were $<ix:nonFraction id="c140632077" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanCostRecognized" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, $<ix:nonFraction id="c140632078" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanCostRecognized" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140632079" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanCostRecognized" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">We have a deferred compensation plan in which all persons serving on the Board of Directors <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>defer all or portions of their annual retainer and meeting fees, with distributions to be paid upon termination of service as a director or specific dates selected by the director. We also have non-qualified deferred compensation programs in which selected officers <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>defer all or portions of salary and bonus payments. The deferred amounts, which totaled&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c140632080" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_BalanceSheetLocationAxis-OtherLiabilitiesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredCompensationLiabilityCurrentAndNoncurrent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140632081" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_BalanceSheetLocationAxis-OtherLiabilitiesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredCompensationLiabilityCurrentAndNoncurrent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.3</ix:nonFraction> million&#160;as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, respectively, are categorized as other liabilities in the Consolidated Balance Sheets. Interest expense was&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c140632083" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="mbwm:InterestExpenseDeferredCompensationPlan" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.1</ix:nonFraction> million during <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, and&#160;less than $<ix:nonFraction id="c140632085" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="mbwm:InterestExpenseDeferredCompensationPlan" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.1</ix:nonFraction> million during&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>&#160;and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">The Mercantile Bank Corporation Employee Stock Purchase Plan of <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> is a non-compensatory plan intended to encourage full- and part-time employees of Mercantile and its subsidiaries to promote our best interests and to align employees&#8217; interests with the interests of our shareholders by permitting employees to purchase shares of our common stock with <ix:nonFraction id="c140632089" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_PlanNameAxis-The2025EmployeeStockPurchasePlanMember" unitRef="Pure" name="mbwm:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardEmployeePayrollDeduction" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">5</ix:nonFraction>% discount through regular payroll deductions. Shares are purchased on the last business day of each calendar quarter at a price equal to the lower of <ix:nonFraction id="c140632090" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_PlanNameAxis-The2025EmployeeStockPurchasePlanMember_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardPurchasePriceOfCommonStockPercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">95</ix:nonFraction>% of the&#160;closing price of our common stock reported on The Nasdaq Stock Market on the <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> business day of each quarter and last business day of the quarter. A total of <ix:nonFraction id="c140632092" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_PlanNameAxis-The2025EmployeeStockPurchasePlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:CommonStockCapitalSharesReservedForFutureIssuance" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">200,000</ix:nonFraction> shares of common stock <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be issued under the existing plan; however, the number of shares <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be adjusted to reflect any stock dividends and other changes in our capitalization. The number of shares issued totaled <ix:nonFraction id="c140632093" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_PlanNameAxis-The2025EmployeeStockPurchasePlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesEmployeeStockPurchasePlans" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">2,356</ix:nonFraction>&#160;in <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, there were approximately <ix:nonFraction id="c140632095" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_PlanNameAxis-The2025EmployeeStockPurchasePlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAvailableForGrant" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">198,000</ix:nonFraction> shares available under our current plan.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">The Mercantile Bank Corporation Employee Stock Purchase Plan of <em style="font: inherit;">2014</em> was&#160;a non-compensatory plan intended to encourage full- and part-time employees of Mercantile and its subsidiaries to promote our best interests and to align employees&#8217; interests with the interests of our shareholders by permitting employees to purchase shares of our common stock through regular payroll deductions. The number of shares issued totaled <ix:nonFraction id="c140632097" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_PlanNameAxis-MercantileBankCorporationEmployeeStockPurchasePlanOf2014Member_StatementEquityComponentsAxis-CommonStockIncludingAdditionalPaidInCapitalMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesEmployeeStockPurchasePlans" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">598</ix:nonFraction> and <ix:nonFraction id="c140632098" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31_PlanNameAxis-MercantileBankCorporationEmployeeStockPurchasePlanOf2014Member_StatementEquityComponentsAxis-CommonStockIncludingAdditionalPaidInCapitalMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesEmployeeStockPurchasePlans" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,194</ix:nonFraction> in <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2024,</em> respectively.&#160;</p>
  </ix:nonNumeric>
  <div>
   &#160;
  </div>
  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:DerivativeInstrumentsAndHedgingActivitiesDisclosureTextBlock" id="c3113624" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">14</em>&#160;</b>&#8211;<b> DERIVATIVES AND HEDGING ACTIVITIES</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">We are exposed to certain risks arising from both business operations and economic conditions. We principally manage the exposure to a wide variety of operational risks through core business activities. Economic risks, including interest rate, liquidity and credit risk, are primarily administered via the amount, sources and duration of assets and liabilities. Derivative financial instruments <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>also be used to assist in managing economic risks.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Derivatives <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> designated as hedges are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> speculative and result from a service provided to certain commercial loan borrowers. We execute interest rate swaps with commercial banking customers desiring longer-term fixed rate loans, while simultaneously entering into interest rate swaps with correspondent banks to offset the impact of the interest rate swaps with the commercial banking customers. The net result is the desired floating rate loans and a minimization of the risk exposure of the interest rate swap transactions. These swap agreements are cross collateralized with the underlying loans.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">As the interest rate swaps associated with this program do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> meet the strict hedge accounting requirements, changes in the fair value of both the commercial banking customer interest rate swaps and the offsetting interest rate swaps with the correspondent banks are recognized directly to earnings. Fees paid to us by the correspondent banks are recognized as noninterest income on our Consolidated Statements of Income on the settlement date.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">The effect of interest rate swaps that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> designated as hedging instruments resulted in expense of less than&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c140632108" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-InterestRateSwapMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OtherNoninterestExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million during the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em> that was recorded in other noninterest expense on our Consolidated Statement&#160;of Income. &#160;We have master netting arrangements with our correspondent banks that allow us to net receivables and payables. The netting agreement also allows us to net related cash collateral received and transferred up to the fair value exposure amount. We have elected to <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> offset these transactions on the Consolidated Balance Sheets. The netting of derivative instruments as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>&#160;is presented in the following table.</p>

   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 9pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">(<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>)</p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">See Note <em style="font: inherit;">16</em>&#160;for a description of the fair value hierarchy as well as a disclosure of levels for classes of financial assets and liabilities.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 9pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">(<em style="font: inherit;">2</em>)</p> </td><td style="width: auto; font-size: 10pt;">It is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> practical to determine the fair value of FHLBI stock due to transferability restrictions&#894; therefore, fair value is estimated at carrying amount.</td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Carrying amount is the estimated fair value for cash and cash equivalents, FHLBI stock, accrued interest receivable and payable, noninterest-bearing checking accounts and securities sold under agreements to repurchase. Security fair values are based on market prices or dealer quotes, and if <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> such information is available, on the rate and term of the security and information about the issuer. Fair value for loans is based on an exit price model as required by ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2016</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">01,</em> taking into account inputs such as discounted cash flows, probability of default and loss given default assumptions. Fair value for deposit accounts other than noninterest-bearing checking accounts is based on discounted cash flows using current market rates applied to the estimated life. The fair values of subordinated debentures, subordinated notes, and FHLBI advances are based on current rates for similar financing. The fair values of interest rate swaps are based on discounted cash flows using forecasted yield curves, along with insignificant unobservable inputs, such as borrower credit spreads. The fair value of other off-balance sheet items is estimated to be nominal.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:FairValueMeasurementInputsDisclosureTextBlock" id="c3113631" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">16</em>&#160;</b>&#8211;<b> FAIR VALUE MEASUREMENTS</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Fair value is defined as the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants. A fair value measurement assumes that the transaction to sell the asset or transfer the liability occurs in the principal market for the asset or liability, or in the absence of a principal market, the most advantageous market for the asset or liability. The price of the principal (or most advantageous) market used to measure the fair value of the asset or liability is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> adjusted for transaction costs. An orderly transaction is a transaction that assumes exposure to the market for a period prior to the measurement date to allow for marketing activities that are usual and customary for transactions involving such assets and liabilities; it is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> a forced transaction. Market participants are buyers and sellers in the principal market that are (i) independent, (ii) knowledgeable, (iii) able to transact and (iv) willing to transact.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">We are required to use valuation techniques that are consistent with the market approach, the income approach and/or the cost approach. The market approach uses prices and other relevant information generated by market transactions involving identical or comparable assets and liabilities. The income approach uses valuation techniques to convert future amounts, such as cash flows or earnings, to a single present amount on a discounted basis. The cost approach is based on the amount that currently would be required to replace the service capacity of an asset (replacement cost). Valuation techniques should be consistently applied. Inputs to valuation techniques refer to the assumptions that market participants would use in pricing the asset or liability. Inputs <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be observable, meaning those that reflect the assumptions market participants would use in pricing the asset or liability developed based on market data obtained from independent sources, or unobservable, meaning those that reflect our own estimates about the assumptions market participants would use in pricing the asset or liability based on the best information available in the circumstances. In that regard, we utilize a fair value hierarchy for valuation inputs that gives the highest priority to quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities and the lowest priority to unobservable inputs. The fair value hierarchy is as follows:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">1:</em> Quoted prices (unadjusted) for identical assets or liabilities in active markets that we have the ability to access as of the measurement date.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">2:</em> Significant other observable inputs other than Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> prices such as quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities in active markets; quoted prices for identical or similar assets or liabilities in markets that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> active; or other inputs that are observable or can be derived from or corroborated by observable market data by correlation or other means.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">3:</em> Significant unobservable inputs that reflect our own estimates about the assumptions that market participants would use in pricing an asset or liability.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">The following is a description of our valuation methodologies used to measure and disclose the fair values of our financial assets and liabilities on a recurring or nonrecurring basis:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Securities available for sale.</i> Securities available for sale are recorded at fair value on a recurring basis. Fair value measurement is based on quoted prices, if available. If quoted prices are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> available, fair values are measured using independent pricing models. Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> securities include U.S. Government agency debt obligations, mortgage-backed securities issued or guaranteed by U.S. Government agencies, and municipal general obligation and revenue bonds. Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> securities include bonds issued by certain relatively small municipalities located within our markets that have very limited marketability due to their size and lack of ratings from a recognized rating service. We carry these bonds at historical cost, which we believe approximates fair value, unless our periodic financial analysis or other information that becomes known to us necessitates an impairment. There was <ix:nonFraction id="c140632135" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_InformationByCategoryOfDebtSecurityAxis-AvailableforsaleSecuritiesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ValuationAllowancesAndReservesBalance" scale="6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> such impairment as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em> or <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>. We have <ix:nonFraction id="c140632137" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_FairValueByFairValueHierarchyLevelAxis-FairValueInputsLevel1Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AvailableForSaleSecuritiesDebtSecurities" scale="6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> securities available for sale.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">16</em>&#160;</b>&#8211;<b> FAIR VALUE MEASUREMENTS </b>(Continued)</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Derivatives.</i> We measure fair value utilizing models that use primarily market observable inputs, such as forecasted yield curves. Insignificant unobservable inputs, such as borrower credit spreads, are also utilized.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Mortgage loans held for sale.</i> Mortgage loans originated and intended for sale in the secondary market are carried at the lower of aggregate cost or market, as determined by outstanding commitments from investors, and are measured on a nonrecurring basis. Fair value is based on independent quoted market prices, where applicable, or the prices for other mortgage whole loans with similar characteristics. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, we determined the fair value of our mortgage loans held for sale to be $<ix:nonFraction id="c140632142" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:MortgagesHeldForSaleFairValueDisclosure" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">17.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140632143" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:MortgagesHeldForSaleFairValueDisclosure" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">16.0</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Loans.</i> We do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> record loans at fair value on a recurring basis. However, from time to time, we record nonrecurring fair value adjustments to collateral dependent loans to reflect partial write-downs or specific reserves that are based on the observable market price or current estimated value of the collateral. These loans are reported in the nonrecurring table below at initial recognition of significant borrower distress and on an ongoing basis until recovery or charge-off. The fair values of distressed loans are determined using either the sales comparison approach or income approach; respective unobservable inputs for the approaches consist of adjustments for differences between comparable sales and the utilization of appropriate capitalization rates.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Foreclosed assets. </i> At time of foreclosure or repossession, foreclosed and repossessed assets are adjusted to fair value less costs to sell upon transfer of the loans to foreclosed and repossessed assets, establishing a new cost basis. We subsequently adjust estimated fair value of foreclosed assets on a nonrecurring basis to reflect write-downs based on revised fair value estimates. The fair values of parcels of other real estate owned are determined using either the sales comparison approach or income approach; respective unobservable inputs for the approaches consist of adjustments for differences between comparable sales and the utilization of appropriate capitalization rates.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">The carrying values are based on the estimated value of the property or other assets. Fair value estimates of collateral on collateral dependent loans and foreclosed assets are review periodically. Our credit policies establish criteria for obtaining appraisals and determining internal value estimates. We <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>also adjust outside appraisals and internal evaluations based on identifiable trends within our markets, such as sales of similar properties or assets, listing prices and offers received. In addition, we <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>discount certain appraised and internal value estimates to address current distressed market conditions. Typically, for real estate dependent loans and foreclosed assets, we assign a discount factor range of <ix:nonFraction id="c140632162" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_CollateralAxis-CommercialRealEstateMember_FinancingReceivableRecordedInvestmentByClassOfFinancingReceivableAxis-RealEstateDependentLoansAndForeclosedAssetsMember_RangeAxis-MinimumMember" unitRef="Pure" name="mbwm:FairValueInputsDiscountFactor" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">25</ix:nonFraction>% to <ix:nonFraction id="c140632163" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_CollateralAxis-CommercialRealEstateMember_FinancingReceivableRecordedInvestmentByClassOfFinancingReceivableAxis-RealEstateDependentLoansAndForeclosedAssetsMember_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" unitRef="Pure" name="mbwm:FairValueInputsDiscountFactor" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">50</ix:nonFraction>%. During <em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em> weighted average discount factors of <ix:nonFraction id="c140632165" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_CollateralAxis-CommercialRealEstateMember_FinancingReceivableRecordedInvestmentByClassOfFinancingReceivableAxis-RealEstateDependentLoansAndForeclosedAssetsMember_RangeAxis-WeightedAverageMember" unitRef="Pure" name="mbwm:FairValueInputsDiscountFactor" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">40.9</ix:nonFraction>%&#160;and&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c140632166" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_CollateralAxis-ResidentialRealEstateMember_FinancingReceivableRecordedInvestmentByClassOfFinancingReceivableAxis-RealEstateDependentLoansAndForeclosedAssetsMember_RangeAxis-WeightedAverageMember" unitRef="Pure" name="mbwm:FairValueInputsDiscountFactor" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">25.8</ix:nonFraction>%&#160;were used for commercial-related and residential-related properties, respectively.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">17</em> &#8211; BUSINESS COMBINATIONS</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em>Mercantile completed its acquisition of Eastern Michigan Financial Corporation, and its wholly owned banking subsidiary, Eastern Michigan Bank, in accordance with the Agreement and Plan of Merger, as amended (the "Merger Agreement") by and between Mercantile, Eastern Michigan Financial Corporation, and Shamrock Merger Sub LLC, a&#160;wholly-owned special purpose subsidiary of Mercantile (&#8220;Merger Sub&#8221;) entered into on <em style="font: inherit;"> July 22, 2025. </em>Pursuant to the Merger Agreement, Eastern Michigan Financial Corporation merged with and into Merger Sub, with Merger Sub continuing as the surviving entity (the &#8220;Merger&#8221;). Immediately following the Merger, and also effective as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em>Merger Sub merged with and into Mercantile, with Mercantile continuing as the surviving entity. The newly acquired Eastern Michigan Bank will operate alongside&#160;Mercantile Bank&#160;until the <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> quarter of <em style="font: inherit;">2027,</em> at which time Mercantile plans to consolidate Eastern Michigan Bank into Mercantile Bank.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">Mercantile accounted for the Eastern Michigan Financial Corporation acquisition as a business combination using the acquisition method of accounting in accordance with ASC <em style="font: inherit;">805,</em> Business Combinations ("ASC <em style="font: inherit;">805"</em>). ASC <em style="font: inherit;">805</em> requires assets purchased and liabilities assumed to be recorded at their respective fair values as of the date of acquisition. Mercantile determined the fair value of loans, core&#160;deposit intangibles, mortgage servicing rights, time deposits, and real property with the assistance of <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party valuations and appraisals.&#160;The following table summarizes the preliminary fair value of the total consideration transferred and the&#160;fair value of identifiable assets acquired,&#160;and liabilities assumed as of the effective date of the transaction:</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:VariableInterestEntityDisclosureTextBlock" id="c3113639" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">18</em>&#160;</b>&#8211;<b> VARIABLE INTEREST ENTITIES</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Variable interest entities ("VIEs") are entities that either have a total equity investment that is insufficient to permit the entity to finance its activities without additional subordinated financial support or whose equity investors lack the characteristics of a controlling financial interest (i.e., ability to make significant decisions, through voting rights, right to receive the expected residual returns of the entity, and obligations to absorb the expected losses of the entity). Variable interest entities can be structured as corporations, trusts, partnerships, or other legal entities. We have relationships with certain variable interest entities related to the issuance of trust preferred securities and our tax credit investments.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">We have <ix:nonFraction id="c140632182" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="mbwm:NumberOfBusinessTrusts" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="INF">five</ix:nonFraction> business trusts that are wholly owned subsidiaries of Mercantile, <ix:nonFraction id="c140632183" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="mbwm:BusinessCombinationDebtAssumedNumberOfTrusts" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="INF">four</ix:nonFraction> of which were assumed by Mercantile in conjunction with the Firstbank Corporation merger in <em style="font: inherit;">2014.</em> A fair value discount of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140632185" contextRef="i_2014-06-01" unitRef="USD" name="mbwm:FairValueDiscountOfSubordinatedDebenturesRelatedToAssumedBusinessTrustsAtTimeAfMerger" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">15.0</ix:nonFraction> million was recorded at the time of the merger, which is being amortized at $<ix:nonFraction id="c140632186" contextRef="d_2014-06-01_2014-06-01" unitRef="USD" name="mbwm:AmortizationOfFairValueDiscountRelatedToSubordinatedDebenturesOfAssumedBusinessTrusts" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.7</ix:nonFraction> million annually over the following <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2014-06-01_2014-06-01" name="mbwm:AmortizationPeriodOfFairValueDiscountRelatedToSubordinatedDebenturesOfAssumedBusinessTrusts" id="c140632187" format="ixt-sec:duryear">21.5</ix:nonNumeric> years, <em style="font: inherit;">11</em>&#160;of which are remaining. Each of the trusts was solely formed to issue preferred securities that were sold in private sales. Through a small common stock investment, we own <ix:nonFraction id="c140632189" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2025-12-31_EquityMethodInvestmentNonconsolidatedInvesteeAxis-FiveBusinessTrustsMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:VariableInterestEntityOwnershipPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="0">100</ix:nonFraction>% of the voting equity shares of each trust. The proceeds from the preferred securities and common stock sales were used by the trusts to purchase Floating Rate Notes issued by Mercantile. The rates of interest, interest payment dates, call features and maturity dates of each Floating Rate Note are identical to its respective Preferred Securities. The net proceeds from the issuance of the Floating Rate Notes were used for a variety of purposes, including contributions to Mercantile Bank as capital to provide support for asset growth and the funding of stock repurchase programs and certain acquisitions.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:45pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 0pt;">The assets, liabilities, operations and cash flows of each trust are solely related to the issuance, administration and repayment of the preferred securities held by <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party investors. We fully and unconditionally guarantee the obligations of each trust and are obligated to redeem the junior subordinated debentures upon maturity. We do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> consolidate the trusts as we are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> the primary beneficiary of these entities because our wholly-owned and indirect wholly-owned statutory subsidiaries do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have the power to direct the activities of the variable interest entity that most significantly impact the variable interest entity&#8217;s economic performance and do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have an obligation to absorb losses or the right to receive benefits that could potentially be significant to the variable interest entity. As such, we do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have a controlling financial interest in the variable interest entities.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">The only significant assets of our trusts are the Floating Rate Notes, and the only significant liabilities of our trusts are the Preferred Securities. The Floating Rate Notes are categorized on our Consolidated Balance Sheets as subordinated debentures and the interest expense is recorded on our Consolidated Statements of Income under interest expense on other borrowings.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> January 26, 2016, </em>we closed on a repurchase of trust preferred securities that were auctioned as part of a pooled collateralized debt obligation (&#8220;Fund&#8221;). The Fund owned $<ix:nonFraction id="c140632196" contextRef="i_2016-01-26_CounterpartyNameAxis-FundMember_SubordinatedBorrowingAxis-MercantileBankCapitalTrustIMember" unitRef="USD" name="mbwm:PreferredSecuritiesOfSubsidiaryTrust" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">11.0</ix:nonFraction> million of the $<ix:nonFraction id="c140632197" contextRef="i_2016-01-26_SubordinatedBorrowingAxis-MercantileBankCapitalTrustIMember" unitRef="USD" name="mbwm:PreferredSecuritiesOfSubsidiaryTrust" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">32.0</ix:nonFraction> million in trust preferred securities that had been issued by Mercantile Bank Capital Trust I. The $<ix:nonFraction id="c140632198" contextRef="d_2016-01-26_2016-01-26_SubordinatedBorrowingAxis-MercantileBankCapitalTrustIMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:PaymentsForRepurchaseOfTrustPreferredSecurities" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">11.0</ix:nonFraction> million in trust preferred securities was retired upon the repurchase, resulting in a commensurate reduction in the related Floating Rate Junior Subordinate Note, leaving $<ix:nonFraction id="c140632199" contextRef="i_2016-01-26_SubordinatedBorrowingAxis-MercantileBankCapitalTrustIMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:JuniorSubordinatedDebentureOwedToUnconsolidatedSubsidiaryTrust" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">21.0</ix:nonFraction> million outstanding.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">The following table depicts our <em style="font: inherit;">five</em> business trusts as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">18</em>&#160;</b>&#8211;<b> VARIABLE INTEREST ENTITIES</b> (Continued)</p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><br/> MCP makes equity investments as a limited liability member in affordable housing projects utilizing the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (&#8220;LIHTC&#8221;) pursuant to Section <em style="font: inherit;">42</em> of the Internal Revenue Code. Mercantile Bank&#160;also invests in multi-investor funds, which in turn invest in projects similar to that of MCP. The purpose of these investments is&#160;to achieve a satisfactory return on capital and to support our banks' community reinvestment initiatives. The activities of the limited liability entities include the identification, development, and operation of multi-family housing that is leased to qualifying residential tenants generally within our banks' primary geographic regions. MCP also makes equity investments via special purpose investment entities as a limited liability member in entities that receive Historic Tax Credits (&#8220;HTC&#8221;) pursuant to Section <em style="font: inherit;">47</em> of the Internal Revenue Code. The purpose of these investments is the rehabilitation of historic buildings with the tax credits provided to incent private investment in the historic cores of cities and towns.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt;">The LIHTC and HTC investment entities are considered VIEs as MCP, or our&#160;banks, whomever is the&#160;holder of the equity investment at risk, does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have the ability to direct the activities that most significantly affect the performance of the entity through voting rights or similar rights. MCP, or our&#160;banks, could absorb losses that are significant to the underlying entities as it has a risk of loss for its capital contributions and funding commitments to each. The general partners, or managing members, are considered the primary beneficiaries as managerial functions give them the power to direct the activities that most significantly impact the entities&#8217; economic performances, and the managing members are exposed to all losses beyond MCP&#8217;s, or our banks', initial capital contributions and funding commitments. We account for these entities using the proportional amortization method with the investment assets amortized in proportion to the income tax credits received in the current period as compared to the total income tax credit benefits expected to be received over the life of the investment.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt;">Equity investments as a limited liability member in LIHTC and HTC investment entities, reported as <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140632574"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140632575">other assets</span></span> in the Consolidated Balance Sheets, totaled $<ix:nonFraction id="c140632206" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AmortizationMethodQualifiedAffordableHousingProjectInvestments" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">51.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140632207" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AmortizationMethodQualifiedAffordableHousingProjectInvestments" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">38.9</ix:nonFraction> million as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, respectively. Unfunded capital commitments, reported as other liabilities in the Consolidated Financial Statements, totaled $<ix:nonFraction id="c140632209" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:QualifiedAffordableHousingProjectInvestmentsCommitment" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">31.1</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140632210" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:QualifiedAffordableHousingProjectInvestmentsCommitment" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">34.4</ix:nonFraction> million as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, respectively.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt;">&#160;</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:RegulatoryCapitalRequirementsUnderBankingRegulationsTextBlock" id="c3113643" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">19</em>&#160;- REGULATORY MATTERS</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">We are subject to regulatory capital requirements administered by federal banking agencies. Capital adequacy guidelines and prompt corrective action regulations involve quantitative measures of assets, liabilities, and certain off-balance sheet items calculated under regulatory accounting practices. Capital amounts and classifications are also subject to qualitative judgments by regulators about components, risk weightings, and other factors, and the regulators can lower classifications in certain cases. Failure to meet various capital requirements can initiate regulatory action that could have a direct material effect on the financial statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">The prompt corrective action regulations provide <em style="font: inherit;">five</em> classifications, including well capitalized, adequately capitalized, undercapitalized, significantly undercapitalized, and critically undercapitalized, although these terms are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> used to represent overall financial condition. If an institution is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> well capitalized, regulatory approval is required to accept brokered deposits. Subject to limited exceptions, <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> institution <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>make a capital distribution if, after making the distribution, it would be undercapitalized. If an institution is undercapitalized, it is subject to close monitoring by its principal federal regulator, its asset growth and expansion are restricted, and plans for capital restoration are required. In addition, further specific types of restrictions <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be imposed on the institution at the discretion of the federal regulator. At year-end <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, our banks were in the well capitalized category under the regulatory framework for prompt corrective action. There are <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> conditions or events since <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em> that we believe have changed our banks' categorizations.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Under the final BASEL III capital rules that became effective on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2015, </em>there is a requirement for a common equity Tier <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> capital conservation buffer of <ix:nonFraction id="c140632222" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="mbwm:CapitalConservationBuffer" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">2.5</ix:nonFraction>% of risk-weighted assets which is in addition to the other minimum risk-based capital standards in the rule. Institutions that do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> meet this required capital buffer will become subject to progressively more stringent limitations on the percentage of earnings that can be paid out in cash dividends or used for stock repurchases and on the payment of discretionary bonuses to senior executive management. The capital buffer requirement was phased in over <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> years beginning in <em style="font: inherit;">2016.</em> The capital buffer requirement raised the minimum required common equity Tier <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> capital ratio to <ix:nonFraction id="c140632227" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="mbwm:CommonEquityTier1RiskBasedCapitalRequiredForCapitalAdequacyToRiskWeightedAssets" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">7.0</ix:nonFraction>%, the Tier <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> capital ratio to <ix:nonFraction id="c140632229" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:TierOneRiskBasedCapitalRequiredForCapitalAdequacyToRiskWeightedAssets" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">8.5</ix:nonFraction>% and the total capital ratio to <ix:nonFraction id="c140632230" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:CapitalRequiredForCapitalAdequacyToRiskWeightedAssets" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">10.5</ix:nonFraction>% on a fully phased-in basis on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2019. </em>We believe that, as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, our banks meet&#160;all capital adequacy requirements under the BASEL III capital rules on a fully phased-in basis.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Federal and state banking laws and regulations place certain restrictions on the amount of dividends our banks can transfer to Mercantile and on the capital levels that must be maintained. At year-end <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, under the most restrictive of these regulations, Mercantile Bank&#160;could distribute $<ix:nonFraction id="c140632232" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:StatutoryAccountingPracticesStatutoryAmountAvailableForDividendPaymentsWithoutRegulatoryApproval" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">12.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and Eastern Michigan Bank could distribute&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c140632233" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-EasternMichiganFinancialCorpMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:StatutoryAccountingPracticesStatutoryAmountAvailableForDividendPaymentsWithoutRegulatoryApproval" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">4.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million to Mercantile as dividends without prior regulatory approval. Our and the ability of our banks&#160;to pay cash and stock dividends is subject to limitations under various laws and regulations and to prudent and sound banking practices. On <em style="font: inherit;"> <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140632576">January 16, 2025</span>, </em>our Board of Directors declared a cash dividend on our common stock in the amount of shareholders of record as of <em style="font: inherit;"> <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140632578">March 7, 2025</span>. </em>On <em style="font: inherit;"> <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140632579">April
