   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, we had the ability to repurchase up to $<ix:nonFraction id="c140632238" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:StockRepurchaseProgramRemainingAuthorizedRepurchaseAmount1" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">6.8</ix:nonFraction> million in common stock shares from time to time in open market transactions at prevailing market prices or by other means in accordance with applicable regulations as part of a $<ix:nonFraction id="c140632239" contextRef="i_2021-05-31" unitRef="USD" name="srt:StockRepurchaseProgramAuthorizedAmount1" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">20.0</ix:nonFraction> million common stock repurchase program announced in <em style="font: inherit;"> May 2021. </em><ix:nonFraction id="c140632240" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockRepurchasedDuringPeriodShares" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">No</ix:nonFraction> shares were repurchased during <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> or <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>. Historically, stock repurchases have been funded from cash dividends paid to us from Mercantile Bank. Additional repurchases <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be made in future periods under the authorized plan or a new plan, which would also likely be funded from cash dividends paid to us from our banks.&#160;The actual timing, number and value of shares repurchased will be determined by us in our discretion and will depend on a number of factors, including the stock price, capital position, financial performance, general market and economic conditions, alternative uses of capital and applicable legal requirements.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Our consolidated capital levels as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> include $<ix:nonFraction id="c140632244" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="mbwm:PreferredSecuritiesOfSubsidiaryTrust" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">48.9</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c140632245" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="mbwm:PreferredSecuritiesOfSubsidiaryTrust" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">48.3</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively, of trust preferred securities. Under applicable Federal Reserve guidelines, the trust preferred securities constitute a restricted core capital element. The guidelines provide that the aggregate amount of restricted core capital elements that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be included in Tier <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> capital must <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> exceed <ix:nonFraction id="c140632248" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="mbwm:MaximumRestrictedCoreElementAllowedInTierOneCapitalPercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">25</ix:nonFraction>% of the sum of all core capital elements, including restricted core capital elements, net of goodwill less any associated deferred tax liability. Our ability to include the trust preferred securities in Tier <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> capital in accordance with the guidelines is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> affected by the provision of the Dodd-Frank Act generally restricting such treatment, because (i) the trust preferred securities were issued before <em style="font: inherit;"> May 19, 2010, </em>and (ii) our total consolidated assets as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2009 </em>were less than $<ix:nonFraction id="c140632251" contextRef="i_2009-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="mbwm:MaximumLevelOfConsolidatedAggregateAssetsAllowingForInclusionOfTrustPreferredSecuritiesInTierOneCapital" scale="9" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-9">15.0</ix:nonFraction> billion. At <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, all $<ix:nonFraction id="c140632253" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="mbwm:TrustPreferredSecuritiesIncludedInTierOneCapital" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">48.9</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140632254" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="mbwm:TrustPreferredSecuritiesIncludedInTierOneCapital" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">48.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively, of the trust preferred securities were included as Tier <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> capital of Mercantile.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">21</em>&#160;</b>&#8211;<b> BUSINESS SEGMENT INFORMATION</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <div style="font-size:10pt">
    <div style="font-family:Times New Roman">
     <div style="font-variant:normal">
       Pursuant to Financial Accounting Standards Codification
      <em style="font: inherit;">280,</em>&#160;
      <i>Segment Reporting,&#160;</i>operating segments represent components of an enterprise for which separate financial information is available that is regularly evaluated by the chief operating decision makers in determining how to allocate resources and assessing performance.
     </div>
    </div>
   </div>
   <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <div style="font-size:10pt">
    <div style="font-family:Times New Roman">
     <div style="font-variant:normal">
       Prior to our acquisition of Eastern Michigan Financial Corporation on
      <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em>our chief operating decision makers, which include&#160;our Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Chief Operating Officer, evaluated interest and noninterest income streams and credit losses from our various products and services, while&#160;expense activities, including interest expense and noninterest expense, were managed, and financial performance was evaluated, on a Company-wide basis. As a result, detailed profitability information for each interest and noninterest income stream was&#160;
      <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> used by&#160;our chief operating decision makers to allocate resources or in assessing performance. Rather, our chief operating decision makers used consolidated net income to assess performance by comparing it to and monitoring against budgeted and prior-year results. This information was&#160;used to manage resources to drive business and net income growth, including investment in key strategic priorities, as well as determine our ability to return capital to shareholders.
     </div>
    </div>
   </div>
   <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <div style="font-size:10pt">
    <div style="font-family:Times New Roman">
     <div style="font-variant:normal">
       Subsequent to our acquisition of Eastern&#160;Michigan Financial Corporation on
      <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em>our chief operating decision makers now evaluate&#160;interest and noninterest income streams, credit losses, expense activities, and financial performance&#160;through our
      <ix:nonFraction id="c140632267" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:NumberOfOperatingSegments" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="INF">two</ix:nonFraction> wholly owned subsidiary banks, Mercantile Bank and Eastern Michigan Bank. Each of these operating segments offer similar products and services, but are managed separately due to different pricing, product demand, and consumer markets.&#160;Both segments derive&#160;interest and noninterest income through their&#160;banking products and services and investment securities.&#160;All of our income relates to our operations in the United States.&#160;Our chief operating decision makers use subsidiary level net income&#160;to assess performance by comparing it to and monitoring against budgeted and prior-year results. This information is&#160;used to manage resources to drive business and net income growth, including investment in key strategic priorities, as well as determine our ability to return capital to shareholders.
     </div>
     <div style="font-variant:normal">
       &#160;
     </div>
    </div>
   </div>
   <div style="font-size:10pt">
    <div style="font-family:Times New Roman">
     <div style="font-variant:normal">
       Segment net income represented&#160;net income on our Consolidated Statements of Income during and for the years ended
      <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em>
      <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and
      <em style="font: inherit;">2023.</em>&#160;Segment assets&#160;represented total assets and goodwill represented total goodwill on our Consolidated Balance Sheets as of
      <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024. </em>Goodwill, core deposit intangible, and total assets by segment as of
      <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>were as follows:
     </div>
